item.title: Why Civic Museums Are Trading Black-Box Galleries for Daylight Stone Atriums
item.description:
KYOTO — Step into the newly reopened municipal wing here at nine in the morning and the first thing you notice is not a security checkpoint or an illuminated wall plaque, but the slow drift of winter sunlight across brushed granite benches.

For forty years, museum renovations followed an orthodoxy imported from black-box theater design: seal every window, tint the glass, and govern every square meter with track lighting. While light-sensitive works on paper still require strict ultraviolet filtering, sculptors and civic curators increasingly view total darkness as an enemy of public life.
